start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:remember-which-tool-was-chosen-for-a-job with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"} and offers [{\"job\": \"keep the rows that match\", \"candidates\": [{\"tool_id\": \"tool:a\", \"label\": \"A\", \"job\": \"does a\"}, {\"tool_id\": \"tool:b\", \"label\": \"B\", \"job\": \"does b\"}]}] and runs [{\"job\": \"keep the rows that match\", \"tool_id\": \"tool:b\", \"state\": \"completed\"}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the tool choices are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:remember-which-tool-was-chosen-for-a-job" with store, and the offers and runs to keep.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: every attempt must give the outcome the intent says, or the run stops and says which.

4. Every later run keeps the new offers and runs through those objects; a run of a tool that was not offered for its job is refused with the store's own words, and the sweep drops a choice nobody has offered or chosen from for 30 days.

worked_examples.title: The tool an AI ran for a job is remembered
worked_examples.ask: Remember that for keeping the rows that match I was offered A and B and ran B.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found the choices kept in the table tool_choice with its keep function, made by an earlier run.
worked_examples.hands_back: kept_ids ["keep the rows that match"], refused [] and found_ids ["keep the rows that match"]; the choice reads chosen_id tool:b at chosen_index 1, and asking again with the same offer writes nothing.
